name: Streaming AI responses
needs: show the AI answer as it's being written
users stare at a spinner while the model thinks
my streamed response arrives all at once in production
summary: Sending the model's answer to the browser piece by piece as it's generated, usually over server-sent events, so people see text within a second instead of waiting for the whole reply. Your server sits in the middle, keeps the API key private, and saves the finished answer.
need_when: Chat or writing features where answers take more than a couple of seconds.
skip_when: The output is structured data your code uses, or the work runs in a background job. Stream progress, not tokens, there.

ways.title: Server-sent events from your backend
ways.how: Call the provider with streaming on, and forward each text chunk to the browser as an SSE event. The browser reads it with fetch and a stream reader, or EventSource for GET requests.
ways.tradeoff: Works with any backend. Proxies and hosts can buffer the stream unless you turn that off.

ways.title: An AI SDK
ways.how: The Vercel AI SDK or the provider's own SDK helpers handle the streaming protocol and the UI state for you.
ways.tradeoff: Least code. Ties your frontend to the SDK's message format.

ways.title: Stream progress from a background job
ways.how: For long tasks, run the AI call in a job and push status updates over SSE or polling.
ways.tradeoff: Survives page reloads and timeouts. Text appears in bigger steps.

prompt:
Stream AI responses to the browser in [feature].

Requirements:
- The browser calls our server, never the provider directly. The API key stays on the server.
- Use the provider's streaming mode and forward text chunks as server-sent events (Content-Type: text/event-stream, Cache-Control: no-cache).
- Turn off response buffering in every proxy in front of the app (for nginx, X-Accel-Buffering: no) and check the host's streaming limits and timeouts.
- If the user closes the page or presses Stop, cancel the upstream request so we stop paying for tokens.
- Save the full answer and token usage to the database when the stream ends, including partial answers when cancelled.
- Show a clear message, not a stack trace, if the stream fails halfway.

Acceptance checks (run each and show me the result):
1. In production, the first words appear within [2] seconds of sending.
2. Pressing Stop ends the provider request (visible in server logs) within a second.
3. Reloading the page shows the saved answer.
4. The API key never appears in browser network requests.
5. Killing the connection mid-answer shows a friendly error and keeps the partial text.
acceptance_checks: In production, the first words appear within [2] seconds of sending.
Pressing Stop ends the provider request (visible in server logs) within a second.
Reloading the page shows the saved answer.
The API key never appears in browser network requests.
Killing the connection mid-answer shows a friendly error and keeps the partial text.
if_you_skip_it: Users think the app froze, streams that work locally arrive in one lump in production, and you pay for answers nobody is reading.
